Plain_English_Definition: Long-end Treasury yields remain elevated or rise even when inflation data would normally support a bond rally, implying fiscal supply, term premium or real-rate pressure is dominating the usual inflation-to-rates transmission.
Typical_Trigger: Benign/soft inflation impulse + weak or absent 10Y/30Y rally; stronger when auctions are weak or the 30Y remains above stress thresholds.
How_To_Interpret: The market is demanding more compensation to fund duration independently of the near-term Fed path.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce reliance on long-duration beta; raise hurdle for expensive long-duration equities; favor cash-flow resilience and shorter-duration expressions.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer that the Fed must hike, or that equities must immediately fall.
Key_Data: CPI/PPI surprises, 2Y/10Y/30Y yields, curve, auctions, real yields.

Plain_English_Definition: Treasury auctions require unusually high yields or show weak demand, confirming duration-supply pressure.
Typical_Trigger: Large auction tail, weak bid-to-cover/indirect demand, or clearing yield near/extending recent extremes.
How_To_Interpret: Primary-market demand is requiring a concession.
Portfolio_Implication: Strengthens fiscal/term-premium warnings and duration caution.
What_Not_To_Infer: One weak auction alone is not a regime change.
Key_Data: 10Y/30Y auction tail, bid-to-cover, indirect/direct demand.

Plain_English_Definition: Near-term Fed expectations ease while the 10Y/30Y fail to follow, separating policy-rate repricing from duration risk.
Typical_Trigger: 2Y/front-end yields fall or hike odds decline while 10Y/30Y stay flat/up.
How_To_Interpret: The curve is being driven by more than the Fed reaction function.
Portfolio_Implication: Treat duration separately from Fed policy; require long-end confirmation for bond adds.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate dovish Fed repricing with a guaranteed long-bond rally.
Key_Data: 2Y, 10Y, 30Y changes; OIS/Fed probabilities.

Plain_English_Definition: Financial conditions tighten through higher long-term yields and funding costs even without a policy-rate hike.
Typical_Trigger: 10Y/30Y or real yields remain high/rise while the policy rate is unchanged or expected to ease.
How_To_Interpret: The bond market is doing part of the central bank's tightening work.
Portfolio_Implication: Penalize refinancing-dependent and long-duration assets; favor strong FCF and low leverage.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat it as identical to a central-bank hike; transmission is asset-specific.
Key_Data: Long yields, real yields, credit spreads, mortgage/corporate rates.

Plain_English_Definition: USD/JPY pressure, Japanese yields and intervention/reserve-management mechanics can feed back into Treasury demand and the US curve.
Typical_Trigger: USDJPY near intervention territory + elevated JGB yields/yield-gap stress + intervention/reserve-flow risk.
How_To_Interpret: An FX event can become a rates-flow event.
Portfolio_Implication: Raise cross-asset fragility monitoring around intervention episodes.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume intervention automatically means Treasury selling or a weaker dollar.
Key_Data: USDJPY, JGBs, US/Japan yield gap, intervention details, reserve flows.

Plain_English_Definition: Refined-product markets tighten materially even when headline crude prices are not signaling equivalent scarcity.
Typical_Trigger: Crack spreads/product prices/inventories tighten while WTI/Brent are flat or less stressed.
How_To_Interpret: Inflation pressure may be hiding downstream in refining/product markets.
Portfolio_Implication: Use diesel/gasoil/gasoline/jet and refinery data in the inflation/energy score.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not conclude energy inflation is benign from crude alone.
Key_Data: Crack spreads, product inventories, refinery utilization/outages, exports.

Plain_English_Definition: Physical supply disruption and demand destruction coexist, creating two-sided nonlinear oil risk.
Typical_Trigger: Constrained flows/inventory draws coexist with weakening demand revisions or usage.
How_To_Interpret: Upside convexity persists while the choke point remains constrained, but normalization can expose a sudden surplus.
Portfolio_Implication: Prefer conditional scenarios and defined-risk expressions; monitor physical buffers.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not extrapolate a high spot price linearly or assume demand destruction guarantees immediate downside.
Key_Data: Hormuz traffic, inventories, SPR releases, demand revisions, curve, oil-on-water.

Plain_English_Definition: Large importers rebuilding strategic/commercial reserves create an additional medium-term source of physical demand.
Typical_Trigger: Announced capacity expansion plus evidence of reserve-filling flows.
How_To_Interpret: Inventory rebuilding is demand first and potential emergency supply later.
Portfolio_Implication: Add to medium-term oil-demand balance, not the daily trading signal.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not count announced capacity as actual demand until filling begins.
Key_Data: Reserve capacity, fill rates, imports, stock policy.

Plain_English_Definition: When normally dissimilar assets move together, decompose each move by its own causal engine before declaring correlations broken.
Typical_Trigger: Unusual co-movement such as tech + energy + USD all rising.
How_To_Interpret: Different assets may be responding to different shocks simultaneously.
Portfolio_Implication: Require causal attribution before using cross-asset divergence as a trade signal.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume unusual correlation equals market dysfunction.
Key_Data: Rates, earnings, physical commodity data, FX, positioning.

Plain_English_Definition: Price recovers faster than investor exposure after a washout, creating forced re-risking and an upside pain trade.
Typical_Trigger: Sharp deleveraging/position cuts followed by price stabilization/rebound while positioning remains light.
How_To_Interpret: The rally can extend because investors are under-positioned rather than crowded.
Portfolio_Implication: Avoid reflexive shorts; use breadth and positioning to judge chase risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer underexposure from narrative alone.
Key_Data: CFTC, prime-broker proxies, dealer positioning, breadth, price.

Plain_English_Definition: Crowding is measured separately across Mag 7, semiconductors, software/TMT and broader AI beneficiaries rather than using one 'AI crowded' label.
Typical_Trigger: Large dispersion in positioning, valuation or breadth across AI sub-groups.
How_To_Interpret: Risk can migrate within the AI complex.
Portfolio_Implication: Size tactical AI exposure by sub-group crowding and relative valuation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume a crowded semiconductor book means all mega-cap technology is crowded.
Key_Data: Prime-broker/CFTC proxies, valuations, breadth, relative strength.

Plain_English_Definition: Tests whether high policy rates are actually restraining borrowing, capital raising, hiring and investment.
Typical_Trigger: Policy rates high but credit demand/capex/issuance remain strong, or vice versa.
How_To_Interpret: The effective neutral/terminal rate may differ from what the policy-rate level alone implies.
Portfolio_Implication: Adjust Fed scenario priors and financing-sensitive asset selection.
What_Not_To_Infer: One Fed speaker's opinion is not itself the state.
Key_Data: Capex, issuance, lending, credit growth, hiring, policy rates.

Plain_English_Definition: Gold and silver are treated primarily through their real opportunity cost rather than headline inflation alone.
Typical_Trigger: Changes in real yields explain bullion better than CPI direction.
How_To_Interpret: High/rising real yields can offset inflation/geopolitical support for metals.
Portfolio_Implication: Require real-yield/USD confirmation before aggressive precious-metals adds.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use 'inflation up = gold up' mechanically.
Key_Data: TIPS real yields, nominal yields, breakevens, USD, bullion.

Plain_English_Definition: A macro release may offer a strong expectation of larger range/volatility without offering a reliable directional edge.
Typical_Trigger: Historical event-day ranges rise while directional hit rate is weak/unstable.
How_To_Interpret: The tradeable edge may be movement, not direction.
Portfolio_Implication: Use defined levels/options structures and post-release cross-asset confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not convert event importance into directional certainty.
Key_Data: Historical event returns/ranges, implied vol, realized vol.

Plain_English_Definition: Higher-beta precious-metals exposure requires bullion stabilization/reclaim plus favorable real-yield/USD transmission.
Typical_Trigger: Bullion holds/reclaims key level; real yields/USD stop working against it; miners stop underperforming.
How_To_Interpret: Macro support must show up in the underlying before miners receive capital.
Portfolio_Implication: Block or limit miner adds until confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not let a strategic gold thesis justify a miner purchase automatically.
Key_Data: Gold, miners/gold relative strength, real yields, USD.

Plain_English_Definition: Proprietary external technical models may frame levels and scenarios but remain source assertions until independently confirmed.
Typical_Trigger: External VC-PMI/cycle/model level is supplied.
How_To_Interpret: Useful for map/levels, not Crown truth.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as secondary support/resistance context only.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not allow proprietary external levels to independently trigger capital.
Key_Data: External model levels + Crown price/flow confirmation.

Plain_English_Definition: Seasonality can adjust prior probabilities but cannot override live evidence or strategic deployment.
Typical_Trigger: Seasonal pattern is historically robust enough to note.
How_To_Interpret: Calendar effects are weak contextual priors.
Portfolio_Implication: Use small confidence adjustment only.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not delay Layer 1 solely because of a seasonal claim.
Key_Data: Seasonal return distributions, conditional samples.

Plain_English_Definition: Research inputs are weighted by provenance, directness, freshness and independence rather than rhetoric or confidence of the author.
Typical_Trigger: Any external research claim enters Crown.
How_To_Interpret: Primary data and independently verifiable evidence receive more weight than narrative assertions.
Portfolio_Implication: Down-weight unverified/leaked/proprietary claims and avoid double counting.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not turn a compelling narrative into a model signal without measurable evidence.
Key_Data: Source metadata, freshness, primary/secondary status.

Plain_English_Definition: Long-term strategic holdings and a separate tactical sleeve coexist and are measured separately.
Typical_Trigger: Always-on portfolio architecture.
How_To_Interpret: Active trading supplements rather than replaces strategic compounding.
Portfolio_Implication: Keep Layer 1 permission and Layer 2/3 performance attribution separate.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not let a tactical loss rewrite the strategic thesis.
Key_Data: Portfolio layer labels and attribution.

Plain_English_Definition: A macro thesis, transmission mechanism and chosen instrument are evaluated separately.
Typical_Trigger: Any proposed or existing trade.
How_To_Interpret: A thesis can be right while the expression is wrong.
Portfolio_Implication: Score thesis, expression, timing and sizing independently; switch expression if transmission fails.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not defend a poor proxy because the macro story still sounds right.
Key_Data: Thesis record, causal channel, instrument behavior.

Plain_English_Definition: For event/geopolitical trades, prefer instruments closest to the causal transmission channel.
Typical_Trigger: Multiple possible expressions exist for a catalyst.
How_To_Interpret: Closer instruments usually carry less basis/transmission risk.
Portfolio_Implication: Favor direct transmission unless costs/liquidity make it inferior.
What_Not_To_Infer: Cheap relative valuation alone is not enough if the instrument is too remote from the shock.
Key_Data: Catalyst, instrument exposure, basis sensitivity.

Plain_English_Definition: Cheap optionality is actionable only when valuation, catalyst, expression and technical context align.
Typical_Trigger: IV attractive versus realized + defined catalyst horizon + suitable instrument + confirmation + bounded downside.
How_To_Interpret: Mispriced convexity can improve payoff asymmetry.
Portfolio_Implication: Permit defined-risk option structures when all filters pass.
What_Not_To_Infer: IV below realized volatility alone is not a buy signal.
Key_Data: IV, realized vol, catalyst calendar, technical state, option structure.

Plain_English_Definition: Expression selection incorporates roll yield, carry, liquidity, spread, tax/operational complexity and implementation cost.
Typical_Trigger: Choosing between futures, ETF/ETC, options or related instruments.
How_To_Interpret: Two instruments with similar beta can have very different realized economics.
Portfolio_Implication: Prefer the cleaner implementation when exposure is equivalent.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not compare only headline price exposure.
Key_Data: Roll curve, expense ratio, spread, liquidity, tax, option terms.

Plain_English_Definition: A technical level is stronger when it aligns with plausible systematic or institutional flow.
Typical_Trigger: Major MA/support/resistance + CTA/trend/dealer/flow threshold in the same region.
How_To_Interpret: The level has a market-mechanics reason to matter.
Portfolio_Implication: Increase tactical confidence modestly; never make it a standalone signal.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume every 200-day moving average has CTA support.
Key_Data: Price levels, CTA proxy, dealer gamma, volume/flow.

Plain_English_Definition: Exit or reduce when the payoff distribution materially deteriorates even before full thesis invalidation.
Typical_Trigger: Underlying softens, contrary supply/news appears, asymmetry worsens, theta/expiry becomes material or transmission changes.
How_To_Interpret: Protecting accrued edge is part of the trade, not an admission of analytical failure.
Portfolio_Implication: Allow profit-taking/reduction before expiry or formal stop.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not wait for the original thesis to become completely false.
Key_Data: Price behavior, catalyst changes, option decay, new information.

Plain_English_Definition: Ranks companies/sectors by dependence on cheap external financing versus internally generated cash flow.
Typical_Trigger: Especially relevant during market-imposed tightening/term-premium stress.
How_To_Interpret: High FCF, low leverage and low refinancing needs are more resilient to elevated long yields.
Portfolio_Implication: Favor self-funded cash generators; penalize highly levered/negative-FCF duration equity.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate all technology with high financing dependency.
Key_Data: FCF, leverage, maturities, interest coverage, capex funding.

Plain_English_Definition: After leverage is purged and price stabilizes, compare implied versus realized volatility and upside flow for asymmetric optionality.
Typical_Trigger: Washout + stabilization + attractive vol + flow/price confirmation.
How_To_Interpret: Forced selling is reduced and convex upside may be underpriced.
Portfolio_Implication: Use limited-risk structures; require confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Unusual calls alone are not a buy signal.
Key_Data: Positioning, IV/RV, options flow, price stabilization.

Plain_English_Definition: Bond volatility rises while equities look calm, often indicating hidden event or rates fragility.
Typical_Trigger: MOVE/bond vol rises while VIX/equity realized vol and volume remain subdued.
How_To_Interpret: Rates are repricing risk before equities.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce complacency and raise event-risk sensitivity.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not automatically short equities.
Key_Data: MOVE, VIX, realized vol, breadth, volume.

Plain_English_Definition: Crowding and squeeze risk are assessed from CFTC, prime-broker positioning and dealer-gamma/options positioning together.
Typical_Trigger: At least two independent positioning sources available.
How_To_Interpret: No single positioning feed should dominate the decision.
Portfolio_Implication: Produce crowding, squeeze, forced-seller and gamma amplification states.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat a leaked prime-broker note as equivalent to direct inventory data.
Key_Data: CFTC, PB research/direct data, dealer gamma proxy.

Plain_English_Definition: Combines macro cycle, liquidity, earnings, valuation and market factors so no single pillar drives allocation.
Typical_Trigger: Each pillar has current score/confidence.
How_To_Interpret: Conflicting evidence should change conviction and size rather than force a binary call.
Portfolio_Implication: Use aggregate conviction to set tactical target around strategic target.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not sell solely because one pillar such as valuation is negative.
Key_Data: Macro, liquidity, earnings, valuation, market confirmation.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates strategic target, deliberate tactical target and accidental weight drift caused by market moves.
Typical_Trigger: Actual weights diverge from intended SAA/TAA weights.
How_To_Interpret: Not every overweight is an active view.
Portfolio_Implication: Rebalance when drift exceeds tolerance or tactical thesis changes.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not mistake price appreciation for a new allocation decision.
Key_Data: Strategic weights, tactical tilts, actual weights.

Plain_English_Definition: Tests whether stronger nominal growth lifts revenues/cash flows faster than discount rates and costs rise.
Typical_Trigger: Inflation/nominal GDP and yields rise together.
How_To_Interpret: Higher inflation/yields are not mechanically bearish if nominal earnings accelerate faster.
Portfolio_Implication: Condition equity sensitivity on margin/cash-flow response.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use 'yields up = equities down' without earnings context.
Key_Data: Nominal GDP, revenue growth, margins, yields.

Plain_English_Definition: Evaluates whether large capex programs are funded sustainably or increasingly rely on debt, issuance, vendor/customer financing or off-balance-sheet structures.
Typical_Trigger: Capex accelerates materially.
How_To_Interpret: Financing quality can change the risk of an otherwise attractive investment boom.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce conviction when capex outpaces internal cash generation and funding quality deteriorates.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat all capex growth as equally bullish.
Key_Data: Capex, FCF, debt issuance, equity issuance, financing structures.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures the macro growth impulse from hyperscaler/data-center/semiconductor investment.
Typical_Trigger: AI infrastructure spending and related construction/equipment accelerate or decelerate.
How_To_Interpret: AI capex can be a meaningful GDP/industrial demand impulse.
Portfolio_Implication: Support infrastructure/semis only when financing and earnings quality also pass.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate capex dollars with future profitability.
Key_Data: Hyperscaler capex, data-center construction, equipment, semis.

Plain_English_Definition: Determines which safe haven should work by tracing the shock through inflation expectations, real yields, USD and liquidity.
Typical_Trigger: Geopolitical/fiscal/financial shock.
How_To_Interpret: Gold, Treasuries and USD can react differently depending on the transmission path.
Portfolio_Implication: Trade the observed transmission rather than the label 'risk-off'.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume every geopolitical shock is bullish for gold or bonds.
Key_Data: Breakevens, real yields, USD, liquidity, gold, Treasuries.

Plain_English_Definition: Scores evidence by source directness, freshness, independence and verifiability.
Typical_Trigger: Every external/non-primary input.
How_To_Interpret: Confidence should reflect evidence quality as well as model fit.
Portfolio_Implication: Use provenance in confidence and double-counting controls.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not give equal weight to primary data and unsourced narrative.
Key_Data: Source metadata.

Plain_English_Definition: Combines Fed balance sheet, Treasury cash/issuance, fiscal flows, bank credit, USD and global liquidity instead of equating liquidity with QE.
Typical_Trigger: Multiple liquidity channels available.
How_To_Interpret: One tightening channel can be offset by another.
Portfolio_Implication: Use net liquidity impulse in allocation, not a single balance-sheet series.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer liquidity solely from Fed assets.
Key_Data: Fed balance sheet, TGA, reserves, credit, USD, global liquidity.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates index strength from the breadth and concentration underlying it.
Typical_Trigger: Cap-weighted index and equal-weight/breadth data diverge.
How_To_Interpret: Strong index returns may coexist with fragile participation.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce conviction when leadership narrows without earnings support.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not call the whole market healthy because the index is at a high.
Key_Data: Equal weight, advance/decline, contribution, earnings breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Combines multiple macro/market models and scores their historical calibration instead of relying on a single forecast.
Typical_Trigger: Multiple independent forecasts/signals exist.
How_To_Interpret: Ensembles reduce model-specific error if independence is real.
Portfolio_Implication: Weight models by out-of-sample calibration and freshness.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not average highly correlated models as if they were independent.
Key_Data: Forecasts, realized outcomes, model correlations.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares slow-moving structural indicators with fast real-time nowcasts to distinguish durable regime shifts from short-lived noise.
Typical_Trigger: Slow and fast macro layers are both available.
How_To_Interpret: Agreement raises confidence; divergence signals transition risk.
Portfolio_Implication: Use divergence to reduce size and demand confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not let one hot release overturn the structural layer.
Key_Data: PMIs, nowcasts, labor/inflation trends, structural data.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures how widely trend signals agree across major asset classes and regions.
Typical_Trigger: Trend states available across equities, bonds, FX and commodities.
How_To_Interpret: Broad agreement is more robust than one-market momentum.
Portfolio_Implication: Use diffusion as confirmation for regime confidence.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not count closely related assets as independent confirmations.
Key_Data: Trend signals across assets.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks whether key asset correlations are normal, unstable or reversing, affecting diversification and hedge reliability.
Typical_Trigger: Rolling correlations shift materially versus historical bands.
How_To_Interpret: Portfolio hedges can fail when correlation regimes change.
Portfolio_Implication: Adjust hedge assumptions and risk budgets.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume historical stock/bond or gold/USD correlation is permanent.
Key_Data: Rolling correlations, covariance.

Plain_English_Definition: Quantifies how far actual weights have drifted from strategic/tactical targets and the economic urgency of rebalancing.
Typical_Trigger: Weight drift exceeds tolerance or concentration rises.
How_To_Interpret: Portfolio risk can change without any new trade.
Portfolio_Implication: Prioritize meaningful, fee-efficient rebalances.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not rebalance tiny deviations that are smaller than transaction costs.
Key_Data: Targets, actual weights, transaction costs.

Plain_English_Definition: Combines money-flow direction/persistence with market breadth to govern equity exposure.
Typical_Trigger: Flow and breadth signals available.
How_To_Interpret: Price moves supported by broad persistent flow are more durable.
Portfolio_Implication: Increase/decrease tactical equity risk gradually with the composite.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use flow alone as a binary timing signal.
Key_Data: Money flow, breadth, persistence.

Plain_English_Definition: Tests whether earnings/fundamental direction agrees with price trend.
Typical_Trigger: Fundamental revisions and price trend both available.
How_To_Interpret: Agreement raises confidence; disagreement warns of narrative/positioning risk.
Portfolio_Implication: Require stronger sizing when both agree.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not short simply because valuation/fundamentals look weak while price remains strong.
Key_Data: Earnings revisions, price trend.

Plain_English_Definition: Sizes risk with awareness that large drawdowns require disproportionately larger gains to recover.
Typical_Trigger: Any proposed position/allocation change.
How_To_Interpret: Drawdown control has nonlinear value.
Portfolio_Implication: Set maximum loss/portfolio drawdown budgets before entry.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not evaluate downside only in percentage points without recovery math.
Key_Data: Position risk, drawdown, volatility.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares equity valuation/earnings yield with prevailing real and nominal rates to measure risk-premium compression.
Typical_Trigger: Valuation and rates both available.
How_To_Interpret: High valuations are more fragile when safe yields are also high.
Portfolio_Implication: Lower permissible overweight as the valuation-rate gap compresses.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use valuation as a short-term timing trigger.
Key_Data: Earnings yield, bond yields, real yields.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks long-run relative rotation between financial assets and hard/real assets.
Typical_Trigger: Relative-strength trends and valuation/capital-cycle evidence align.
How_To_Interpret: Leadership can migrate for years rather than weeks.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as strategic/tactical tilt prior, not daily trade trigger.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not extrapolate one commodity spike into a secular rotation.
Key_Data: Commodity/equity ratios, valuations, capex, inflation regime.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures dependence of index returns/earnings on a small number of names or themes.
Typical_Trigger: Contribution concentration, breadth or valuation dispersion becomes extreme.
How_To_Interpret: The index can remain strong while underlying fragility rises.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce concentration and demand stronger confirmation for crowded leaders.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer imminent crash from concentration alone.
Key_Data: Index contribution, breadth, valuation, earnings concentration.

Plain_English_Definition: Composite of leverage, issuance, options/speculative activity and valuation excess.
Typical_Trigger: Multiple speculative indicators become extreme.
How_To_Interpret: Fragility rises when leverage and narrative reinforce each other.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce risk budget at extremes; require price confirmation before acting.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not short solely because speculation is high.
Key_Data: Margin debt, options, issuance, unprofitable growth, valuation.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks how past returns influence capex, capacity and future supply.
Typical_Trigger: Producer profitability/capex/spare capacity data available.
How_To_Interpret: Underinvestment can create future scarcity; high returns eventually attract supply.
Portfolio_Implication: Use with inventories/curve before allocating to producers/commodities.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume high prices automatically mean near-term new supply.
Key_Data: Capex, depreciation, spare capacity, inventories, curve.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares corporate-insider behavior with public-market enthusiasm.
Typical_Trigger: Reliable insider buying/selling data diverge materially from market sentiment.
How_To_Interpret: Insiders may provide a slow caution/confirmation signal.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as low-frequency overlay only.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use noisy insider transactions as a direct trade trigger.
Key_Data: Insider transactions, valuation, sentiment.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures whether thematic capex/valuation enthusiasm is outrunning actual cash-flow growth and estimate breadth.
Typical_Trigger: Capex/valuation accelerate faster than FCF/revisions.
How_To_Interpret: Transformative technology can still be a poor investment at the wrong economics.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce permissible overweight unless price/breadth/revisions remain strong.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not conclude the technology itself is invalid.
Key_Data: Capex, FCF, valuation, revisions, breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Assesses labor-market resilience through hiring, quits, claims and unemployment duration rather than layoffs alone.
Typical_Trigger: Low-hire/low-fire dynamics or changing labor turnover.
How_To_Interpret: A labor market can look stable while its ability to absorb displaced workers deteriorates.
Portfolio_Implication: Raise recession sensitivity when hiring buffer erodes.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate low layoffs with a healthy labor market.
Key_Data: Hiring rate, quits, claims, duration.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares payroll growth with the jobs needed to absorb current labor-supply growth.
Typical_Trigger: Payroll and labor-supply/participation/immigration estimates available.
How_To_Interpret: A fixed '100k jobs' threshold becomes obsolete when labor supply changes.
Portfolio_Implication: Interpret payroll strength relative to contemporaneous labor supply.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use one historical payroll threshold across regimes.
Key_Data: Payrolls, participation, population/immigration, labor force.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates generalized inflation from a headline driven by a small number of categories.
Typical_Trigger: Category-level CPI/PCE data available.
How_To_Interpret: Broad inflation is more persistent than concentrated shocks.
Portfolio_Implication: Adjust inflation persistence and Fed reaction-function confidence.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer broad overheating from one or two volatile categories.
Key_Data: CPI/PCE category diffusion/contribution.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks shock transmission from tariff/energy/import costs through margins into consumer prices and second-round effects.
Typical_Trigger: Cost shock occurs.
How_To_Interpret: Announcement, import cost, margin absorption and consumer pass-through are distinct stages.
Portfolio_Implication: Update inflation risk as the shock moves through the pipeline.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume announced tariffs equal immediate CPI.
Key_Data: Tariffs, import prices, margins, producer/consumer prices.

Plain_English_Definition: Scores a macro release for revisions, temporary distortions, sampling/collection issues and event contamination.
Typical_Trigger: Any major macro release.
How_To_Interpret: Not every print deserves equal weight.
Portfolio_Implication: Discount noisy releases in event-aware capital decisions.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat first print as ground truth when reliability is low.
Key_Data: Revisions, weather/strikes, response rates, methodology.

Plain_English_Definition: Uses conditional inflation/labor/growth states to map possible Fed paths rather than relying on a single dot-plot point estimate.
Typical_Trigger: Macro states and market pricing available.
How_To_Interpret: Policy is a conditional probability distribution.
Portfolio_Implication: Maintain multiple paths and update weights as data change.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat SEP median as a committee promise.
Key_Data: Labor, inflation, growth, market pricing, Fed communication.

Plain_English_Definition: Distinguishes durable productivity/business-formation/labor-reallocation growth from temporary nominal or fiscal impulses.
Typical_Trigger: Productivity, business formation and investment composition available.
How_To_Interpret: Growth quality affects how long an expansion can persist without inflation.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as strategic macro prior.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer quality solely from headline GDP.
Key_Data: Productivity, formation, investment, labor reallocation.

Plain_English_Definition: Uses high-frequency survey internals to estimate current growth before official GDP data.
Typical_Trigger: PMI output/orders and related nowcast variables available.
How_To_Interpret: Faster than quarterly data, but survey-sensitive.
Portfolio_Implication: Use for event/regime updates with reliability checks.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not override hard data after large survey distortions.
Key_Data: PMI output, orders, services/manufacturing.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks PMI input costs, output prices and delivery stress as an early inflation pipeline.
Typical_Trigger: PMI price components available.
How_To_Interpret: Survey price pressure can lead official inflation.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as forward inflation input.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat supplier delays as inflation without decomposing the cause.
Key_Data: PMI input/output prices, delivery times.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares new orders with current output to identify future acceleration or backlog exhaustion.
Typical_Trigger: PMI orders/output available.
How_To_Interpret: Orders leading output can signal future production changes.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as fast growth momentum input.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use the gap without inventory/backlog context.
Key_Data: PMI orders, output, backlogs.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures how widely expansion/contraction is distributed across sectors/regions.
Typical_Trigger: Sector/region PMI data available.
How_To_Interpret: Broad improvement is more durable than one-sector strength.
Portfolio_Implication: Raise/lower confidence in the nowcast.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat one large sector as the whole economy.
Key_Data: Sector/regional PMIs.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates delivery delays caused by strong demand/capacity pressure from delays caused by exogenous supply disruption.
Typical_Trigger: Delivery times deteriorate.
How_To_Interpret: The same PMI component can imply demand strength or supply shock.
Portfolio_Implication: Route to growth or inflation risk depending on cause.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret slower deliveries mechanically as stronger demand.
Key_Data: Delivery times, orders, inventories, shipping/disruption data.

Plain_English_Definition: Uses PMI employment/hiring intentions to identify labor turning points before official payrolls.
Typical_Trigger: PMI employment data available.
How_To_Interpret: Survey labor components can lead official employment.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as secondary labor confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not replace payroll/claims data with PMI alone.
Key_Data: PMI employment, hiring intentions.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks export orders, shipping and manufacturing breadth to gauge global trade momentum.
Typical_Trigger: Trade-sensitive survey/physical data available.
How_To_Interpret: Global trade turns can affect cyclicals, EM and commodities.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as cross-asset growth input.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer global trade from one country's exports.
Key_Data: Export orders, shipping, trade volumes.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares input-cost pressure with firms' ability to raise output prices.
Typical_Trigger: PMI input and output price indices available.
How_To_Interpret: Costs rising faster than selling prices can compress margins.
Portfolio_Implication: Use in earnings/margin risk scoring.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat high input costs as negative if pricing power is equally strong.
Key_Data: PMI input/output prices.

Plain_English_Definition: Down-weights PMI signals distorted by lockdowns, weather, strikes, stockpiling or abnormal delivery mechanics.
Typical_Trigger: Known temporary shock affects survey responses.
How_To_Interpret: Survey level may not represent underlying demand.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce nowcast confidence temporarily.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not discard the whole survey permanently.
Key_Data: Event metadata, PMI internals.

Plain_English_Definition: Layer 1 capital is authorized for deployment; tactical conditions may change pace but not cancel permission indefinitely.
Typical_Trigger: Strategic floor/underweight/schedule authorizes capital.
How_To_Interpret: Strategic objective has priority over tactical perfection.
Portfolio_Implication: Deploy in fee-efficient tranches within max deferral.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not keep cash indefinitely because Layer 3 is neutral.
Key_Data: Strategic target, cash, schedule.

Plain_English_Definition: Layer 2/3 capital is not currently authorized because timing, expression, event or friction conditions fail.
Typical_Trigger: One or more tactical gates fail.
How_To_Interpret: Tactical risk is withheld while strategic rules remain separate.
Portfolio_Implication: Wait for specified confirmation or use alternative expression.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret as a blanket portfolio risk-off signal.
Key_Data: Technical/event/expression/friction gates.

Plain_English_Definition: The setup may be attractive directionally but the current price is too extended relative to the defined entry plan.
Typical_Trigger: Price runs beyond acceptable entry zone without a new base/retest.
How_To_Interpret: Risk/reward deteriorated even if thesis remains valid.
Portfolio_Implication: Wait for consolidation/retest or another expression.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not convert FOMO into a larger order.
Key_Data: Price distance, ATR, support/resistance.

Plain_English_Definition: Long-term Treasury yields are above a framework stress threshold or rising fast enough to pressure duration-sensitive assets.
Typical_Trigger: Typical Crown threshold includes the 30Y around/above 5%, subject to context.
How_To_Interpret: Long discount rates are a portfolio headwind independent of front-end policy.
Portfolio_Implication: Raise hurdle for duration and financing-dependent assets.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume immediate equity collapse.
Key_Data: 10Y/30Y yields and changes.

Plain_English_Definition: Equities rise while breadth, volatility, credit or rates confirmation remains weak.
Typical_Trigger: Index up with warning signals such as VIX up, narrow breadth or long-end stress.
How_To_Interpret: Price is constructive but internally vulnerable.
Portfolio_Implication: Stay invested selectively; avoid leverage/chasing.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate fragility with a confirmed bear market.
Key_Data: Index, breadth, VIX, credit, rates.

Plain_English_Definition: Macro backdrop and positioning/flow point in opposing directions.
Typical_Trigger: Macro score and positioning score have materially opposite signs.
How_To_Interpret: Near-term price can diverge from macro fair value.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce conviction and wait for price/cross-asset confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not choose one side automatically.
Key_Data: Macro composite, positioning.

Plain_English_Definition: Markets price materially tighter policy/financial conditions than previously expected.
Typical_Trigger: Front-end yields/OIS/Fed probabilities reprice higher.
How_To_Interpret: Risk assets face a higher discount-rate hurdle.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce tactical duration/growth sensitivity.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer long-end behavior without term-premium analysis.
Key_Data: 2Y/OIS/Fed pricing.

Plain_English_Definition: Dealer positioning is estimated to be short gamma, which can amplify directional moves.
Typical_Trigger: Dealer-gamma proxy below zero/threshold.
How_To_Interpret: Hedging flows may reinforce price movement.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce leverage; expect wider intraday range.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat gamma sign as directional forecast.
Key_Data: Dealer gamma proxy/options positioning.

Plain_English_Definition: Mega-cap positioning/valuation is crowded enough to raise unwind risk.
Typical_Trigger: Positioning and/or valuation reaches extreme historical percentile.
How_To_Interpret: Good news may have fewer incremental buyers.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce chase size; use breadth/earnings confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not short solely because a name is crowded.
Key_Data: Positioning, valuation, price.

Plain_English_Definition: AI-related exposure is crowded enough to raise fragility or squeeze/unwind risk.
Typical_Trigger: AI positioning composite extreme.
How_To_Interpret: Positioning can dominate short-horizon reactions.
Portfolio_Implication: Size down and differentiate sub-groups.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat all AI assets as equally crowded.
Key_Data: Positioning, options, valuation.

Plain_English_Definition: Copper long positioning is historically crowded.
Typical_Trigger: CFTC/flow percentile extreme.
How_To_Interpret: Upside can persist but reversal sensitivity rises.
Portfolio_Implication: Avoid late leverage and monitor liquidation risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not short solely because positioning is crowded.
Key_Data: CFTC/flow.

Plain_English_Definition: Infrastructure is outperforming relevant broad-market benchmarks on a sustained basis.
Typical_Trigger: Relative-strength trend positive.
How_To_Interpret: Physical-capex/defensive real-asset leadership may be broadening.
Portfolio_Implication: Supports infrastructure tilt if fundamentals/valuation agree.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer macro cause from price alone.
Key_Data: Relative strength, breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Gold underperforms industrial/cyclical assets, indicating weaker defensive monetary leadership.
Typical_Trigger: Gold-relative ratios trend lower.
How_To_Interpret: Market may prefer growth/real-activity exposures over monetary hedge.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce tactical gold enthusiasm unless other gold drivers confirm.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not abandon strategic gold solely on relative performance.
Key_Data: Gold/industrial ratios.

Plain_English_Definition: AI hardware/infrastructure bottleneck beneficiaries outperform broader AI/software exposure.
Typical_Trigger: Semis/hardware/infrastructure relative strength leads.
How_To_Interpret: Scarce physical capacity is capturing more economics.
Portfolio_Implication: Favor bottleneck beneficiaries when earnings/financing confirm.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not extrapolate indefinitely after vertical moves.
Key_Data: Relative strength, earnings, capex.

Plain_English_Definition: Leadership is changing within risk assets without evidence of a broad systemic liquidation.
Typical_Trigger: Sector dispersion rises while credit/breadth/systemic stress remain contained.
How_To_Interpret: Weakness in one theme may be rotation rather than market breakdown.
Portfolio_Implication: Rotate selectively rather than de-risking everything.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not call every leadership break a crash.
Key_Data: Sector relative strength, credit, breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: A small number of mega-cap stocks account for an unusually large share of index performance or earnings.
Typical_Trigger: Contribution/concentration exceeds historical bands.
How_To_Interpret: Index-level diversification is weaker than it appears.
Portfolio_Implication: Use equal-weight/breadth checks and diversify satellite risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer immediate downside.
Key_Data: Index contribution, earnings concentration.

Plain_English_Definition: Gold fails to provide expected diversification during a specified risk shock.
Typical_Trigger: Risk-off/hedge environment occurs but gold does not respond as expected.
How_To_Interpret: The shock is transmitting through yields/USD/liquidity differently.
Portfolio_Implication: Use safe-haven transmission analysis before adding.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume the long-term gold thesis is permanently invalid.
Key_Data: Gold, yields, USD, risk assets.

Plain_English_Definition: Long-duration government bonds fail to rally during an equity/risk shock.
Typical_Trigger: Risk assets weaken but long yields do not fall/bonds do not rise.
How_To_Interpret: Inflation/term-premium/fiscal stress may be dominating.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce assumed bond hedge ratio; consider shorter duration.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not conclude bonds are permanently useless diversifiers.
Key_Data: Equities, Treasury returns/yields, inflation expectations.

Plain_English_Definition: Macro signals are mixed and the economy/markets appear to be transitioning between clearer regimes.
Typical_Trigger: Major macro pillars disagree or their momentum is changing.
How_To_Interpret: Conviction should be lower than in a clean expansion/recession/inflation regime.
Portfolio_Implication: Use smaller tactical tilts and demand cross-asset confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not force a single macro narrative.
Key_Data: Growth, inflation, labor, liquidity, rates.

Plain_English_Definition: Price action is broadly range-bound/neutral rather than in a clean trend.
Typical_Trigger: Trend/momentum and support-resistance evidence are mixed.
How_To_Interpret: Directional edge is limited; relative value and staged entries matter more.
Portfolio_Implication: Avoid large directional tactical bets; focus on levels and diversification.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret neutral as bearish.
Key_Data: Price trend, breadth, volatility.

Plain_English_Definition: Layer 1 is authorized at least at the minimum strategic deployment amount.
Typical_Trigger: Strategic schedule/underweight and cash availability meet the floor.
How_To_Interpret: Capital should be deployed fee-efficiently within the maximum deferral window.
Portfolio_Implication: Execute the strategic floor even if tactical timing is not perfect.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not let a tactical block cancel the strategic floor.
Key_Data: Strategic allocation, cash, schedule.

Plain_English_Definition: A scheduled/systematic investment window is currently open.
Typical_Trigger: Current date falls inside the predefined deployment window.
How_To_Interpret: Systematic capital has permission to deploy subject to operational/compliance checks.
Portfolio_Implication: Execute according to the systematic schedule.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not convert a routine window into a discretionary market-timing exercise.
Key_Data: Calendar, systematic allocation rules.

Plain_English_Definition: Participation is widening beyond the previous narrow leadership group.
Typical_Trigger: Advance/decline, equal-weight and sector participation improve.
How_To_Interpret: The rally is becoming less dependent on a few names.
Portfolio_Implication: Support broader equity exposure if credit/rates remain compatible.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume broadening is complete after one session.
Key_Data: Breadth, equal-weight, sector participation.

Plain_English_Definition: Market gains are increasingly concentrated in fewer stocks/sectors.
Typical_Trigger: Breadth/equal-weight deteriorate while cap-weighted index holds up.
How_To_Interpret: Index strength is becoming more fragile.
Portfolio_Implication: Favor quality and reduce concentrated tactical chase risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not call an immediate market top solely from narrowing breadth.
Key_Data: Breadth, equal-weight, contribution.

Plain_English_Definition: A major release has occurred but the cross-asset reaction has not yet stabilized enough for a directional conclusion.
Typical_Trigger: Release is out but rates/FX/equities/commodities are giving mixed or early signals.
How_To_Interpret: The first price impulse may be noise or positioning rather than durable information.
Portfolio_Implication: Wait for the defined cross-asset sequence before releasing tactical capital.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not trade the headline alone.
Key_Data: Release surprise, 2Y/10Y/30Y, curve, USD, breadth, vol.

Plain_English_Definition: AI-related assets are recovering, but leadership is uneven and breadth/earnings confirmation is still required.
Typical_Trigger: Price rebound occurs with mixed participation across AI sub-groups.
How_To_Interpret: Recovery is real but not yet robust enough for indiscriminate AI exposure.
Portfolio_Implication: Prefer selective quality/earnings-backed expressions; avoid blanket chase.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret index rebound as uniform AI health.
Key_Data: AI subgroup breadth, earnings revisions, positioning, price.

Plain_English_Definition: Multiple risk-sensitive assets and market internals are confirming improving risk appetite.
Typical_Trigger: Equities/credit/breadth/volatility align constructively.
How_To_Interpret: Risk-taking is broadly being rewarded.
Portfolio_Implication: Allow normal tactical risk subject to valuation and event gates.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not ignore concentration or term-premium stress.
Key_Data: Equities, credit, breadth, volatility, USD/rates context.

Plain_English_Definition: Multiple risk-sensitive assets and internals are confirming defensive behavior.
Typical_Trigger: Equities/credit/breadth weaken while volatility/defensive demand rise.
How_To_Interpret: Capital preservation has higher short-term value.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce tactical beta and favor robust hedges/liquidity.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume every defensive asset will work; check safe-haven transmission.
Key_Data: Equities, credit, vol, breadth, safe havens.

Plain_English_Definition: A tactical order is blocked because estimated round-trip transaction cost is too large and no sufficient expected edge has been documented.
Typical_Trigger: Fixed commission/spread burden exceeds the configured threshold and expected edge is unavailable.
How_To_Interpret: The idea may be valid, but the proposed size is economically inefficient.
Portfolio_Implication: Increase order size, wait for a better setup, or reject the trade.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret this as a bearish view on the asset.
Key_Data: Order notional, commissions, spread, expected edge.

Plain_English_Definition: The VWCE cash-flow-matched counterfactual cannot be calculated because contribution dates/amounts have not been supplied.
Typical_Trigger: No usable cash_flow_ledger.csv is present.
How_To_Interpret: The audit is incomplete on opportunity cost from idle cash.
Portfolio_Implication: Provide contribution dates and amounts; other audit components continue normally.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume Crown beat or lost to DCA without this baseline.
Key_Data: Cash contribution ledger.

Plain_English_Definition: Strategic capital remained uninvested beyond the permitted schedule/deferral despite available cash and strategic authorization.
Typical_Trigger: Strategic permission open + available cash + no execution beyond max deferral.
How_To_Interpret: Tactical caution has improperly overridden Layer 1.
Portfolio_Implication: Flag as process failure and quantify delay cost.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not confuse deliberate cash allocation with accidental underdeployment.
Key_Data: Strategic target, cash, permission date, trades.

Plain_English_Definition: Entry rules rejected the asset near support and later rejected it as too extended, causing the framework to miss the entire move.
Typical_Trigger: No starter at reversal/support + later NO_CHASE after a material rally.
How_To_Interpret: Confirmation requirements are too binary or too slow.
Portfolio_Implication: Use staged starter/add logic and measure false negatives.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not lower all entry standards; repair the sequencing rule.
Key_Data: Signals, price path, execution history.

Plain_English_Definition: Crown eventually authorized a trade only after a material portion of the move had already occurred.
Typical_Trigger: Initial WAIT/BLOCK followed by BUY/ADD after a threshold forward move.
How_To_Interpret: Risk control may have become expensive opportunity cost.
Portfolio_Implication: Measure price/unit loss from delay and recalibrate the confirmation gate.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume every delayed entry is bad; avoided drawdowns matter too.
Key_Data: Signal history, trade date, price path.

Plain_English_Definition: Crown had a buy/add thesis but no execution occurred and the asset subsequently moved materially in the expected direction.
Typical_Trigger: Expired buy-like signal + no matching trade + positive forward return above threshold.
How_To_Interpret: A false negative or execution failure occurred.
Portfolio_Implication: Attribute to timing, strategic veto, expression or user override.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not count tiny/noisy moves as missed opportunities.
Key_Data: Signal history, trades, forward returns.

Plain_English_Definition: Crown withheld a trade and the subsequent price path validated that decision.
Typical_Trigger: WAIT/NO_CHASE/BLOCK + no execution + materially adverse forward return.
How_To_Interpret: The gate added value by avoiding a loss.
Portfolio_Implication: Credit the relevant gate, net of any later opportunity cost.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not reward avoidance if strategic capital was still required elsewhere.
Key_Data: Signal history, price path.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures whether the user's action differing from Crown's recommendation added or destroyed value.
Typical_Trigger: Actual execution conflicts with recorded Crown action and enough forward data exist.
How_To_Interpret: Discretion and model performance can be separated empirically.
Portfolio_Implication: Track override alpha/drag rather than judging anecdotes.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat one successful override as proof the framework is useless.
Key_Data: Signal, execution, forward returns.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks the economic cost/benefit of following, delaying or overriding Crown signals.
Typical_Trigger: Persistent signal IDs can be matched to actual trades and subsequent returns.
How_To_Interpret: Decision-process compliance becomes measurable.
Portfolio_Implication: Use in calibration of gates and execution discipline.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not optimize behavior to maximize hit rate at the expense of risk-adjusted outcomes.
Key_Data: Signal ledger, trade ledger, counterfactual.

Plain_English_Definition: Signal weights are being evaluated historically but are not yet allowed to alter live allocations because the sample is too small.
Typical_Trigger: Resolved sample below configured minimum (20 resolved 20-day observations by default).
How_To_Interpret: The framework is learning without overfitting live capital.
Portfolio_Implication: Report suggested weights but keep live weights unchanged.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not promote a signal after a handful of wins.
Key_Data: Resolved signals, forward outcomes.

Plain_English_Definition: One or more required data inputs are missing, stale, inferred or failed to retrieve, reducing confidence without forcing fabricated values.
Typical_Trigger: Price/API/input or reconciliation failure occurs.
How_To_Interpret: The run remains usable but affected outputs must be interpreted with lower confidence.
Portfolio_Implication: Mark affected modules and exclude inferred items from performance attribution.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not fill missing data with guesses.
Key_Data: Data freshness, API errors, reconciliation flags.

Plain_English_Definition: Every signal declares whether it is a condition, timing, sizing or invalidation input, together with horizon and expiry.
Typical_Trigger: Any signal enters the canonical registry.
How_To_Interpret: Condition indicators change risk budgets and confirmation thresholds; only compatible timing signals authorize tactical execution.
Portfolio_Implication: Reject or down-weight signals missing class/horizon/expiry; prevent condition warnings from silently becoming trades.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat a vulnerability indicator as a trade trigger without a compatible timing signal.
Key_Data: Canonical signal registry, signal metadata.

Plain_English_Definition: Decomposes long Treasury yields into expected short rates, inflation/growth fair value, term premium, supply/intermediation and positioning/technicals.
Typical_Trigger: A material move occurs in 10Y/30Y yields or a Treasury auction.
How_To_Interpret: Different components imply different persistence and asset transmission.
Portfolio_Implication: Route the move to Fed, fiscal/term-premium, liquidity or positioning logic before changing duration risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not label every yield increase as hawkish Fed or fiscal stress.
Key_Data: OIS/2Y, inflation/growth, term-premium model, auction/dealer data, positioning.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures funding-market stress through reserves/QT, TGA/ON RRP, SOFR-IORB, SRF, swap spreads and Treasury-basis dislocations.
Typical_Trigger: Funding metrics move away from normal corridor/arbitrage relationships.
How_To_Interpret: The system may be experiencing balance-sheet scarcity even when broad macro liquidity looks adequate.
Portfolio_Implication: Raise tactical fragility and distinguish funding support from solvency support.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume a liquidity backstop fixes earnings or solvency problems.
Key_Data: Reserves, TGA, ON RRP, SOFR-IORB, SRF, swap spreads, basis.

Plain_English_Definition: Scores whether independent downstream markets confirm, contradict or give mixed evidence about one causal thesis.
Typical_Trigger: One event or macro thesis has observable reactions in rates, USD, credit, volatility, breadth and relevant commodities.
How_To_Interpret: Aligned independent evidence raises confidence; contradiction reduces it.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as a tactical confirmation/veto and record each independent evidence item.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not count correlated descendants of one shock as independent votes.
Key_Data: Rates, USD, credit, vol, breadth, commodities, regional FX.

Plain_English_Definition: Maintains one canonical event/cause and treats downstream market moves as evidence rather than separate shocks.
Typical_Trigger: Several signals arise from the same underlying event.
How_To_Interpret: Prevents double-counting one narrative five times.
Portfolio_Implication: Assign common event_id/cause_id and count independent confirmations only.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not increase confidence merely because the same cause appears in several derived indicators.
Key_Data: Event ledger, signal provenance graph.

Plain_English_Definition: Every event narrative decays unless refreshed by physical, fundamental or market confirmation.
Typical_Trigger: Event headline occurs or an event flag is created.
How_To_Interpret: Unconfirmed narratives lose decision weight through time.
Portfolio_Implication: Store half-life, next review and expiry; move through shock/repricing/confirmation/persistence/reversal/expiry phases.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not leave event flags permanently active because the story remains in the news.
Key_Data: Event timestamps, physical confirmation, price closes, policy updates.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares the dollar reaction with the direction implied by rates, risk and the event narrative.
Typical_Trigger: USD reaction diverges from the expected macro transmission.
How_To_Interpret: The narrative may be incomplete, crowded or wrong.
Portfolio_Implication: Lower tactical confidence and investigate relative growth/rates, safe-haven demand and positioning.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume USD always follows US yields or always behaves as a safe haven.
Key_Data: DXY/major FX, rates, risk assets, event direction.

Plain_English_Definition: Uses Asian equities, semiconductors and FX as an overnight lead for global/AI/EM risk, requiring US-session confirmation.
Typical_Trigger: KOSPI/Taiwan semis, KRW/TWD/CNH, Nikkei and US futures move coherently overnight.
How_To_Interpret: Asia can reveal the first transmission of semiconductor, China or carry stress.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as execution evidence for VFEA/semis/global beta, not as a standalone allocation trigger.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume an overnight move will persist into the US session.
Key_Data: KOSPI, Taiwan semis, KRW/TWD/CNH, Nikkei, US futures.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures breadth, magnitude and persistence of EPS/sales revisions and guidance across company, sector and market levels.
Typical_Trigger: Point-in-time analyst revisions are available over 1w/4w/13w horizons.
How_To_Interpret: Broad persistent upward revisions are stronger than a single headline beat.
Portfolio_Implication: Increase fundamental conviction only when revisions are broad and post-event price confirms.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not count repeated forecasts from the same analyst as independent breadth.
Key_Data: EPS/sales revisions, guidance, sector breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Evaluates backlog by growth, book-to-bill, funded/contracted share, duration visibility and margin conversion, penalized for concentration/cancellation/financing risk.
Typical_Trigger: A company or sector cites backlog/order growth.
How_To_Interpret: Backlog matters only to the extent it is funded, deliverable and profitable.
Portfolio_Implication: Prefer durable funded backlog with cash/margin conversion; cap weak-quality backlog.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat a large headline backlog as automatically bullish.
Key_Data: Backlog, book-to-bill, contracts, concentration, cancellation terms, margins/FCF.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates AI physical-capacity suppliers from hyperscaler/platform spenders and detects divergent economics.
Typical_Trigger: Supplier revisions/backlog/pricing and spender capex/FCF/financing move differently.
How_To_Interpret: Suppliers can benefit from capex while spenders face monetization or financing pressure.
Portfolio_Implication: Prefer the stronger side of the AI capital cycle rather than treating AI as one trade.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer that strong AI capex makes both suppliers and spenders equally attractive.
Key_Data: Supplier revisions/backlog, capex, FCF, debt/equity issuance, buybacks, monetization.

Plain_English_Definition: Combines real/nominal 10Y momentum, 2Y/Fed repricing, credit spreads, energy-inflation impulse and growth/value relative weakness.
Typical_Trigger: Concentrated growth or semiconductors are being evaluated tactically.
How_To_Interpret: Elevated score means the discount-rate/funding hurdle is rising faster than growth leadership can absorb.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce Layer 2/3 concentrated-growth size while leaving Layer 1 strategic investing intact.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not automatically sell all technology because yields rise.
Key_Data: 2Y, 10Y, real yields, credit, energy, growth/value relative strength.

Plain_English_Definition: Basing/accumulation stage after a decline, with flat/range-bound price and unreliable trend signals.
Typical_Trigger: Trend/range evidence matches a Stage 1 base.
How_To_Interpret: Opportunity is forming but directional conviction is low.
Portfolio_Implication: Preserve capital, build watchlists, use smaller tactical risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not force breakout trades before confirmation.
Key_Data: Trend, range, moving averages, breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Confirmed advancing trend with higher highs/lows and improving leadership/breadth.
Typical_Trigger: Trend and breadth confirm an advance.
How_To_Interpret: Trend-following tactics have their best environment.
Portfolio_Implication: Own leaders, buy controlled pullbacks and allow normal tactical size.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not chase vertically extended entries.
Key_Data: Trend, breadth, relative strength, volatility.

Plain_English_Definition: Topping/distribution stage where momentum fades, failed breakouts rise and leadership narrows.
Typical_Trigger: Distribution/breadth/leader evidence deteriorates while headline price remains elevated.
How_To_Interpret: The market is fragile even before the index fully breaks.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce tactical size, tighten risk and close chase gates.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not liquidate Layer 1 solely because Stage 3 is detected.
Key_Data: Breadth, equal-weight, leaders, downside volume, vol/credit.

Plain_English_Definition: Established declining trend with lower highs/lows and selling pressure dominating.
Typical_Trigger: Price/trend evidence confirms sustained decline.
How_To_Interpret: Long tactical expectancy is poor except for explicit countertrend setups.
Portfolio_Implication: Avoid normal Layer 2/3 longs, use defensives/cash and separate short-risk budget if enabled.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not cancel scheduled Layer 1 investing merely because the tactical stage is Stage 4.
Key_Data: Trend, breadth, relative strength, volatility.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures deterioration beneath a still-elevated index through narrowing breadth, leader lower highs, failed breakouts, downside volume, volatility divergence, defensive rotation and credit non-confirmation.
Typical_Trigger: Late-stage trend character weakens before headline index trend fails.
How_To_Interpret: The trend may be mature and vulnerable to correlation/breadth deterioration.
Portfolio_Implication: Scale Layer 2 exposure down and close chase gates.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use distribution risk as an automatic market-top call.
Key_Data: Breadth, leaders, volume, vol, defensives, credit.

Plain_English_Definition: Scales tactical size by market stage, volatility, event risk, liquidity and entry extension rather than fixed euro amount alone.
Typical_Trigger: Any Layer 2/3 position is proposed.
How_To_Interpret: The same thesis deserves less capital in noisier or later-stage regimes.
Portfolio_Implication: Apply multiplicative risk reducers bounded at the approved base risk.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not let confidence multipliers raise risk above the base cap.
Key_Data: Stage, realized/implied vol, event/liquidity state, extension.

Plain_English_Definition: Classifies an entry as ATTRACTIVE, ACCEPTABLE, EXTENDED or CHASE_BLOCKED using trend distance, ATR extension, gaps/consecutive moves and post-event move already realized.
Typical_Trigger: A tactical entry is evaluated.
How_To_Interpret: Entry quality is separate from thesis quality.
Portfolio_Implication: Use normal/staged/zero tactical size according to state and wait for reset if extended.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use oscillator extremes alone as the entry decision.
Key_Data: 20/50DMA distance, ATR, breakout distance, gaps, event move.

Plain_English_Definition: Classifies a sharp drawdown as LIQUIDATION_LIKELY, FUNDAMENTAL_LIKELY, MIXED or INSUFFICIENT_DATA using speed, volatility, flows/OI/margin, macro/physical confirmation and rebound behavior.
Typical_Trigger: Large abrupt move occurs in a commodity or risk asset.
How_To_Interpret: Forced selling and fundamental impairment have different re-entry logic.
Portfolio_Implication: Use liquidation classification to change cooling-off/confirmation rules, never as an automatic buy.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not average down merely because a move looks forced.
Key_Data: Price speed, vol, OI, margin/flows, macro/physical data, rebound.

Plain_English_Definition: Maintains separate structural gold-hedge support and tactical gold-pressure scores.
Typical_Trigger: Gold is considered for strategic or tactical allocation.
How_To_Interpret: Structural support can remain high while tactical conditions are poor.
Portfolio_Implication: Allow planned strategic tranches while blocking tactical chase/miner adds when tactical pressure is high.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not mechanically net structural and tactical scores into one number.
Key_Data: Fiscal/reserve/geopolitical structural inputs; real yields/USD/trend/positioning tactical inputs.

Plain_English_Definition: Requires both monetary and industrial confirmation for silver and penalizes disagreement between them.
Typical_Trigger: Silver allocation/trade is evaluated.
How_To_Interpret: Silver behaves as both monetary metal and industrial/high-beta asset.
Portfolio_Implication: Use smaller size and larger volatility haircut than gold; demand dual confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat silver as simply cheaper gold.
Key_Data: Gold regime, real yields/USD, manufacturing/orders, copper/industrial metals, flows/breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Measures oil tightness from curve, inventories, refinery/product stress, shipping/tanker stress, supply disruption, Brent-WTI and demand validation.
Typical_Trigger: Oil/geopolitical risk is evaluated.
How_To_Interpret: Physical confirmation distinguishes durable tightness from headline premium.
Portfolio_Implication: Route confirmed stress into inflation/duration risk; do not automatically chase energy equities.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use spot crude alone as the physical-stress measure.
Key_Data: Curve, inventories, cracks/products, shipping, disruption, demand.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks Henry Hub, TTF and JKM separately using storage, flow surprises, cargo pull, export utilization, weather and terminal/shipping concentration.
Typical_Trigger: Regional gas stress is evaluated.
How_To_Interpret: Gas is regional; basis and infrastructure determine transmission.
Portfolio_Implication: Apply regional/sector effects rather than a global-gas blanket signal.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not collapse Henry Hub, TTF and JKM into one score.
Key_Data: Regional prices/spreads, storage, feedgas, terminals, shipping, weather.

Plain_English_Definition: Models energy shock through products/freight/fertilizer into breakevens, rates, USD, growth equities and consumer stress.
Typical_Trigger: Commodity/energy shock occurs.
How_To_Interpret: Second-order transmission matters more than the headline crude move.
Portfolio_Implication: Adjust inflation/rates/growth risk only when downstream transmission confirms.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not infer persistent inflation from oil direction alone.
Key_Data: Products, freight, fertilizer, breakevens/swaps, 2Y/10Y, consumer stress.

Plain_English_Definition: Evaluates whether an instrument actually delivers the intended sleeve exposure versus unintended factor betas and regime instability.
Typical_Trigger: Any ETF/ETC/future is assigned to a sleeve.
How_To_Interpret: Low-purity instruments can contaminate allocation and attribution.
Portfolio_Implication: Cap sizing and disclose dominant unintended factor; prefer cleaner alternative.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not trust an instrument label as proof of economic exposure.
Key_Data: Intended/unintended betas, tracking error, structure, regime stability.

Plain_English_Definition: Short-dated implied volatility rises ahead of a known catalyst.
Typical_Trigger: Front-end vol steepens/rises ahead of event.
How_To_Interpret: Price drift may reflect hedging and premium rather than directional conviction.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce tactical size and avoid chasing pre-event drift.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not interpret higher IV as directional information.
Key_Data: VIX1D/VIX9D, event calendar, skew/gamma.

Plain_English_Definition: Implied volatility collapses after an event, temporarily reducing hedging pressure and supporting price.
Typical_Trigger: Event passes and short-dated IV falls sharply.
How_To_Interpret: Mechanical support may appear even without new fundamental information.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as temporary support only with breadth/rates confirmation.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not treat IV crush as a durable bullish thesis.
Key_Data: Event IV, realized move, breadth, rates.

Plain_English_Definition: Dealer hedging is estimated to reinforce price direction when gamma is negative.
Typical_Trigger: Gamma proxy is materially negative and price moves through relevant levels.
How_To_Interpret: Move distribution can widen and intraday momentum can self-reinforce.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce leverage and widen expected range while preserving hard max loss.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not use gamma sign as a directional forecast by itself.
Key_Data: Gamma proxy, spot, options OI/vol surface.

Plain_English_Definition: Estimated positive dealer gamma tends to dampen movement and increase range/pinning behavior.
Typical_Trigger: Gamma proxy materially positive near large strikes/levels.
How_To_Interpret: Hedging flows may oppose price movement.
Portfolio_Implication: Avoid chasing breakouts without confirmation; favor range-aware execution.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume positive gamma prevents a fundamental breakout.
Key_Data: Gamma proxy, strikes, spot, vol.

Plain_English_Definition: Forced covering appears largely complete and continuation requires new fundamental or discretionary buyers.
Typical_Trigger: Gamma/delta reversal and positioning normalize after a squeeze while breadth/dispersion fail to confirm.
How_To_Interpret: Mechanical buying impulse is fading.
Portfolio_Implication: Close chase gates and demand new confirmation for further tactical adds.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not automatically short simply because a squeeze is mature.
Key_Data: Gamma/delta, positioning, breadth, dispersion.

Plain_English_Definition: Index calm masks large single-stock dispersion and low implied correlation, creating fragility if correlations suddenly rise.
Typical_Trigger: Single-stock/index vol contrast and dispersion are extreme while index vol remains subdued.
How_To_Interpret: Diversification inside the index can disappear quickly in a correlation shock.
Portfolio_Implication: Retain defensives and reduce concentrated tactical beta.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not equate low index VIX with low stock-level risk.
Key_Data: Single-stock/index IV, dispersion, implied correlation, breadth.

Plain_English_Definition: Constituent correlations jump higher, causing index-level moves to accelerate and diversification to weaken.
Typical_Trigger: Implied/realized correlation rises sharply from a low-dispersion regime.
How_To_Interpret: Many positions can move together unexpectedly.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce concentration, reassess hedge ratios and retain liquidity/defensives.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not assume historical stock/bond or sector correlations remain valid.
Key_Data: Implied/realized correlation, dispersion, index/constituent vol.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares pre-event implied move/skew/gamma with post-event realized move, IV crush, gap retention, cross-asset response and 1/3/5-session drift.
Typical_Trigger: Major macro/earnings event has defined option/event data.
How_To_Interpret: Separates volatility edge from directional/persistence edge.
Portfolio_Implication: Use to evaluate event trade quality and whether the move is retained or reversed.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not judge event success only by the first candle.
Key_Data: Expected move, realized move, IV, gap, rates/USD, drift.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks short-lived liquidity effects from Treasury settlements, tax dates and cash-management operations through reserves/repo plumbing.
Typical_Trigger: Large bill/coupon settlement or tax/quarter-end cash movement occurs.
How_To_Interpret: Can amplify markets for roughly 1-3 sessions without changing the macro liquidity regime.
Portfolio_Implication: Use as tactical timing amplifier with hard expiry unless broader liquidity confirms.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not promote a one-day settlement effect into a permanent liquidity regime.
Key_Data: Settlement calendar, TGA, reserves, ON RRP, SOFR-IORB, SRF/repo.

Plain_English_Definition: Tracks OPEX/VIX expiry, index rebalances, month/quarter-end, CTA threshold proximity and vol-control direction.
Typical_Trigger: Known mechanical-flow window approaches.
How_To_Interpret: Price can temporarily deviate from fundamentals due to forced/mechanical flow.
Portfolio_Implication: Lower confidence in short-horizon price signal and apply expiry; never change strategic targets directly.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not invent flow direction when exposure data are unavailable.
Key_Data: OPEX/expiry/rebalance calendar, CTA thresholds, vol-control estimates.

Plain_English_Definition: Confirms that a Layer 2/3 trade has a complete pre-trade record: layer, setup, entry, invalidation, stop/time stop, max loss, units, event/liquidity state and re-entry rule.
Typical_Trigger: Any Layer 2/3 order is proposed.
How_To_Interpret: A complete ticket makes the decision auditable and prevents post-hoc rule changes.
Portfolio_Implication: Block incomplete discretionary Layer 2/3 execution.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not waive required fields because conviction feels high.
Key_Data: Trade ticket fields.

Plain_English_Definition: Prevents a failed short-term trade from silently becoming a tactical or strategic holding.
Typical_Trigger: A trade is stopped, invalidated or exceeds its original horizon.
How_To_Interpret: Changing the holding horizon changes the thesis and risk contract.
Portfolio_Implication: Close/reassess and create a new decision if another layer genuinely wants the asset.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not migrate a losing trade to avoid realizing a loss.
Key_Data: Trade layer, horizon, invalidation, postmortem.

Plain_English_Definition: Maps Layer 3 risk permission to NORMAL, CAUTION, RECOVERY or LOCKOUT using tactical-sleeve drawdown/recovery evidence.
Typical_Trigger: Tactical sleeve drawdown/recovery thresholds are crossed.
How_To_Interpret: Risk should fall mechanically as drawdown deepens rather than increasing to recover faster.
Portfolio_Implication: Apply calibrated multipliers approximately 1.0/0.5/0.25/0 and require review before re-risking.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not apply tactical drawdown lockout to scheduled Layer 1 purchases.
Key_Data: Tactical NAV/drawdown, recovery days, compliance.

Plain_English_Definition: Temporarily prohibits same-instrument re-entry after a stop unless a pre-authorized re-entry setup existed before the first trade.
Typical_Trigger: Layer 3 trade stops out or is invalidated.
How_To_Interpret: Cooling-off reduces revenge trading and repeated whipsaw.
Portfolio_Implication: Wait until the next decision bar/defined cooldown or pre-authorized setup.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not create a new re-entry rule after the stop simply to get back in.
Key_Data: Stop timestamp, setup registry, decision bars.

Plain_English_Definition: Flags repeated incomplete tickets, oversizing, stop widening, time-stop breach, layer migration, cooldown breach or event-gate bypass.
Typical_Trigger: One or more execution-discipline rules are violated.
How_To_Interpret: Process quality is deteriorating even if recent P&L happens to be positive.
Portfolio_Implication: Reduce allowed Layer 3 risk and require review until compliance improves.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not reward rule-breaking because one trade made money.
Key_Data: Execution tickets, trades, postmortems, compliance ledger.

Plain_English_Definition: Interprets releases using actual-consensus surprise, prior revision, composition, pre-event pricing, policy-path change and cross-asset confirmation, with direction/confidence/half-life.
Typical_Trigger: Major macro release occurs.
How_To_Interpret: The path/reaction function matters more than a good/bad headline label.
Portfolio_Implication: Use the complete surprise-to-path record before releasing tactical capital.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not ignore revisions or pre-event expectations.
Key_Data: Actual/consensus/prior, components, OIS/path, rates/USD/cross-asset response.

Plain_English_Definition: Compares current rates, priced 3m/6m/12m policy paths, growth/inflation surprises, guidance and balance-sheet direction between two regions.
Typical_Trigger: Currency/regional relative value is evaluated.
How_To_Interpret: Expected path changes often matter more than the spot rate gap.
Portfolio_Implication: Use in FX/regional equity relative-value and translation analysis.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not trade currencies on current policy-rate differentials alone.
Key_Data: Policy curves, surprises, guidance, balance sheets.

Plain_English_Definition: Separates local-asset return from currency contribution to the EUR investor and identifies hedge-relevant FX risk.
Typical_Trigger: Portfolio holds non-EUR assets or unhedged funds.
How_To_Interpret: The same local-market outcome can produce different EUR returns.
Portfolio_Implication: Report local return, FX return, total EUR return and hedge note separately.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not confuse an FX hedge decision with an asset-allocation decision.
Key_Data: Holding currency mix, hedge status, local/FX returns.

Plain_English_Definition: Scores ex-ante probabilistic forecasts with Brier/log loss, realized move and false-positive rate by regime, using point-in-time data.
Typical_Trigger: Sufficient resolved forecast ledger observations exist.
How_To_Interpret: Calibration reveals whether confidence levels deserve trust.
Portfolio_Implication: Keep reweighting in shadow mode until sample is adequate; exclude revised/unavailable data.
What_Not_To_Infer: Do not judge model quality from a few memorable calls.
Key_Data: Forecast ledger, outcomes, timestamps, regimes.
